title: Base change for the right adjoint of a proper flat derived pushforward
statement: Let Y and Y' be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let g:Y'\to Y be a morphism, and let f:X\to Y be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and of finite presentation. Form the cartesian square X'=X\times_Y Y' with projections g_X:X'\to X and f':X'\to Y'. Let a and a' be right adjoints to Rf_* and Rf'_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Then for every K in the quasi-coherent derived category of Y there is a canonical base-change isomorphism a'(Lg^*K)\cong Lg_X^*a(K) in the quasi-coherent derived category of X'.

proof.text: Apply the restriction-compatibility statement [lem-sc-proper-flat-right-adjoint-restriction-open] to f and to its base change f'. It says explicitly that formation of both right adjoints and of the base-change morphism commutes with restriction to quasi-compact affine opens on either Y or Y'. Hence, using affine-open covers and the locality of isomorphisms in D_QCoh, it suffices to prove the assertion when Y'\to Y is a morphism of affine schemes.

proof.text: For affine Y'\to Y, the hypotheses of Tag 0AA8 hold: f is proper, and flatness of f gives Tor independence with every g; finite presentation is the case (1) hypothesis. Thus [lem-sc-proper-flat-right-adjoint-affine-basechange] identifies the canonical map Lg_X^*a(K) \to a'(Lg^*K) as an isomorphism for every K. The restriction identifications from the preceding step transport this affine isomorphism to the original covers, so the global base-change map is an isomorphism.
